cause: a weight that is not a function of the value alone, recomputed at drop; and an attribute classified by a path a kind of attribute does not have
whys: why the count grew: put added the tree's whole bytes, drop took off half
why half: `heap_bytes` divided by the tree's strong count, and at drop the thread's tree cache held the tree too
why divided: so two parses sharing a tree count it once; the count was taken to be of weighed values only, and nothing says who may hold a file's tree

why a drift and not a one-off: the table keeps a running sum and no per-value record, so any weight that differs between put and drop is kept or lost for good until an lru pass sums again, and a pass runs only past a budget

why called new: the build VM's table lists what fails there and not on main; the Mac had never run `-p hir --lib` at 8e9c163248, so a failure that predates the commit (or is the Mac's) read as the commit's

why `cfg` was not inert: the tree gives `cfg(..)` and `cfg_attr(..)` their own meta kinds with a predicate and no path, and `is_inert` was written against `Attr::path` alone; its test had no cfg'd assoc item until today
property: an account kept as a sum of recomputed weights; a red test attributed by date
class: a running count whose debit is recomputed instead of recorded (the same class as a refcount decremented by a value read later); and blame by coincidence in time, with no run on the same machine before the change
prevention: Done: `Parse::heap_bytes` is the whole tree whoever holds it, the same at put and at drop; the test's failure now prints each grown ingredient after each of the six rounds, so a step per round and a step once are told apart from the message. `is_inert` tells `CfgMeta` (inert) and `CfgAttrMeta` (not) by kind.
